title: The Muted Piano Late Night Sessions videos
summary: Quarantined, he started posting nightly soft-pedal improvisation videos on Facebook, added donation links, and was moved by a 97-year-old viewer and young pianists.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: the end of it. So I stayed I think about four weeks without doing nothing even. Because the first two weeks I was supposed to be quarantined. Right? So I just was locked into the bedroom. My wife was sleeping on the sofa you know. So then the two weeks went by and life was back in a way, so at least I could go to the grocery store with the mask. And so I think another ten days went by and then I told myself, you know, I cannot just keep doing just not playing anymore, not performing anymore. And so I started making every night, one or two videos and posting them on Facebook. Mostly improvisation based on standards. And so because you see my wife also has been working from home, what happened, the only chance for me to really record these clips was at night. And so I had to use the mute on the piano. And so I called it “The Muted Piano Late Night Sessions.” I did I think 112 of them.
Wow. Are you talking about the soft pedal?

Yeah. The soft pedal that some upright pianos have, that normally is the middle pedal. You press it down and there is a felt that goes in between the strings and the hammers and it creates like that a very soft, muffled sound that is actually very nice. And I found it in a way very, very jazzy. And so I started recording these videos. I would put on a suit every night with a jacket and a tie you know, and it started almost like a joke. And then people seemed to like it. And they kept watching these videos and I put there a link for donations in case someone — and I have to be honest with you, at first the donation option I didn’t even consider it. And then I had some fans writing to me privately saying please post a link for it. And so I didn’t know how to do it, because I didn’t know what PayPal was. I didn’t know what Venmo was, still, because I’m not technological, I’m old school, I get paid either with checks and sometimes with a little cash. So I figured out the PayPal and Venmo and I put it there and now every now and then people will drop something. But you know it’s not the money, I think I’m very grateful for people donating some money but the greatest satisfaction came when I got an email from a gentleman that is 97 years old, 97. And he said that I wake up every morning looking for your Mute email. You know? And so I said that’s it, no matter what, I’m going to do it. Because this one person, that is 97 years old that loves music and gets up in the morning and wants to see my late night video. You know that means more than anything to me. Then I started to get mails from young piano players, you know? Asking me for suggestions and expressing their desire to learn and so that was another strong motivation. I said I’m happy to show my hands and the way I improvise and all this material is there for anyone to use the way they want. You know if all of a sudden there are ten young piano players that start the so-called stealing phrases and techniques, that’s what they are supposed to do. I am happy for that. I hope all this music that I’ve been posting has helped someone to alleviate all the psychological stress. © Fillius Jazz Archive -3-
